title: A Microfluidic-based Electrochemical Biochip for Label-free DNA Hybridization Analysis
protocol: Rinse a blank 4” silicon wafer (prime grade quality) with acetone, methanol, and isopropanol (“AMI” clean).
Rinse the isopropanol from the wafer with deionized water (DI) followed by drying with N2 gun.
Grow a 1 µm thick SiO2 passivation layer with plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) tool.
Deposit a 200 Å thick layer of chromium followed by a 2,000 Å thick layer of gold with a DC sputtering tool.
Spin “PR1” positive photoresist to create uniform film ~1.6 µm thick.
Pre-bake the wafer for 1 min at 100 °C on a hot plate.
Expose the wafer with 190 mJ/cm2 at 405 nm wavelength through a photomask.
Develop the wafer for 30 sec in 352 developer and rinse the wafer with DI and dry with N2 gun.
Etch the gold with gold etchant for 1.5 min.
Etch the chromium with chromium etchant for ~30 sec.
Rinse the wafer with DI and dry with N2 gun.
Strip the photoresist with “AMI” clean procedure.
Clean the wafer with 4:1 H2SO4:H2O2 mixture (“Piranha” clean) for 1 min.
Rinse the wafer with DI and dry with N2 gun.
Spin “PR2” positive photoresist at 3,000 rpm, accelerating at 1,000 rpm/sec for 30 seconds.
Pre-bake the wafer for 1 minute at 100 °C on a hot plate.
Expose the wafer with 30 mJ/cm² at 405 nm wavelength through a photomask.
Bake the wafer for 45 seconds at 125 °C on a hot plate.
Flood expose the wafer with 1,000 mJ/cm² at 405 nm wavelength without a photomask.
Develop the wafer for 2 minutes in a 6:1 AZ400K developer solution and rinse with DI water.
Dry the wafer with an N₂ gun.
Deposit a 400 Å thick layer of titanium followed by a 1,600 Å thick layer of platinum using an E-beam evaporation system.
Lift off photoresist in an ultrasonicated acetone bath for 5 minutes and rinse with acetone and isopropanol.
Rinse the wafer with DI water and dry it with an N₂ gun.
Expose the wafer with 2,500 mJ/cm² at 405 nm wavelength through a photomask.
Post-bake the wafer by ramping up to 95 °C at 300 °C/hr and hold temperature for 10 min on a hot plate.
Develop the wafer for 10 min in Propylene Glycol Monomethyl Ether Acetate (PGMEA) developer.
Rinse the wafer with isopropanol.
Dry the wafer with an N2 gun.
Prepare a 10:1 polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) mixture (20 g of elastomer, 2 g of curing agent).
Degas the PDMS mixture in a vacuum chamber for 20 min.
Define an enclosure around the mold wafer with aluminum foil.
Slowly pour the uncured PDMS over the mold.
Bake the mold with the PDMS in a box furnace using two-step baking parameters: step one – 5 min ramp up from room temperature to 80 °C, and step two – hold at 80 °C for 17 min.
Peel away the PDMS from the mold and place it on aluminum foil.
Cut the assay chips with a surgeon knife.
Define holes in the PDMS with a biopsy punching tool.
Manually align the PDMS assay channels with the working electrodes on the electrochemical chip.
Attach flexible tubing (OD 0.087", ID 0.015") to plastic elbow or straight connectors using a short flexible tube as an adapter (OD 0.1875", ID 0.0625").
Connect adapters to each of the hole-punched inlets in the device.
Connect a syringe to the tubing.
Place the syringe in a syringe pump.
Change the set of syringe, tube, and connector as required by the procedure step in section 3.
Introduce each solution slowly into the channel at a flow rate of 200 µl/hr until the whole channel is filled.
Functionalize each vertical microchannel with a different ssDNA probe sequence.
Fill each microchannel with an incubation solution containing 10 mM phosphate buffer, 100 mM NaCl, 10 µM TCEP, and 1 µM probe ssDNA.
Incubate the microchannels for 1 hour.
Rinse the microchannels with PBS.
Fill the microchannels with a solution of 1 mM MCH in a buffer containing 10 mM PBS, 100 mM NaCl, and 1.395 mM TCEP.
Incubate the microchannels for 1 hour.
Rinse the microchannels with PBS.
Lift off the PDMS.
Rotate the PDMS to a horizontal orientation.
Place down the PDMS to expose separate rows of reaction chambers each containing unique counter and reference electrodes.
Fill the microchannels with control measurement solution of 4x concentrated SSC buffer.
Incubate for 20 minutes.
Fill the microchannels with a 5 mM ferricyanide / 5 mM ferrocyanide solution in PBS.
Record impedance values using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for different frequencies.
Set EIS parameters: frequency range from 1 MHz to 0.1 Hz, 10 data points per decade, 25 mV amplitude, and 5 mV polarization versus the reference electrode.
Repeat impedance measurement for each working electrode in the microchannels.
Fill the microchannels with a solution containing 4x concentrated SSC buffer and 1 µM of target ssDNA.
Incubate the filled microchannels for 20 minutes.
Measure DNA hybridization according to step 3.4.
